Counsel for respondent no. 3 insurance company had submitted during course of arguments that there is contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner also as 03 persons were riding on motorcycle no. DL5SCX-4423, which was driven by one of the victim namely Sachin Batham, who was having only Learner's License and the present petitioner Suraj and one Sonu were pillion riding the same.

He had further submitted that petitioner Suraj has admitted in the cross- examination that they were three (persons sitting)
on the motorcycle of Sachin (driver of the motorcycle) and at the time of accident they were overtaking the bus from the left side.

He has further submitted that at least 50% amount be deducted towards contributory negligence out of the amount to be awarded as compensation to the petitioner as he was triple riding the same despite knowing the fact that it was in violation of traffic rules & regulations.

Though the respondent no. 3 had not examined any witness qua the factum of contributory negligence, however, Ld. Counsel for the petitioner has submitted during course of arguments that factum of triple riding is not disputed.

Furthermore, the petitioner, while deposing as PW1, has admitted in his cross- examination that Sachin Batham was driving the motorcycle, they were three (persons sitting) on the motorcycle and Sachin was having learner's licence at the time of accident.
Furthermore it is stated by PW1 that at the time of accident, they were driving at left side of the road and he admitted that at the time of accident they were overtaking the bus from the left side.

As per the DAR Ex. PW1/A (colly) also, the driver namely Sachin of the motorcycle bearing no.
DL-5SCX-4423

was not possessing valid Licence at the time of accident and was triple riding the same and as such was challaned for the offences u/s 3/181 & u/s MACT No. 517/2023 Suraj Vs.

Sita Rani, owner of the said vehicle, who had given the said vehicle to the petitioner Sachin for driving the same, was also challaned u/s 5/180 of M.V. Act. However, I do not find any force in the argument of Ld. Counsel for respondent no. 3 that all the three riders of the motorcycle were not wearing helmet at the time of accident as except for bald suggestion, no material to this effect has been proved on record.
Furthermore, the petitioner/PW1 has denied the suggestion that none of of them were wearing helmet at the time of accident.

Since the petitioner Suraj was pillion riding the motorcycle as one of the three persons on the motorcycle and driver Sachin was not possessing a valid driving licence, despite knowing the fact that same were in violation of traffic rules and regulations and since the motorcycle driver tried to overtake the bus from left side instead of right side, which is the correct side, therefore by application of the principles of Preponderance of Probability, the petitioner Suraj is also held liable for contributory negligence and as such 25% (Twenty Five Percent) shall be deducted from the amount, to be awarded as compensation to the petitioner, towards contributory negligence.
